audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows disagree with the already-audited mirror: Level 3 and Level 6 read Skill here while the mirror gives both to Darius, and Two+ items reads Darius while the mirror gives it to Sylas.
audit.why: Level 6 is his level before it is yours — five Hemorrhage stacks plus Noxian Guillotine is a kill he can execute on his own terms, while your stolen copy has to be set up. Two items in, Sylas is the better teamfighter.
audit.corrected: Level 3 and Level 6 read Darius, Two+ items reads Sylas, with phases[4].why and whys[4] rewritten so the chart and the paragraph agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is named as the clock the whole lane runs on and never numbered anywhere.
audit.why: It is 26s at rank 1 and still 16s maxed — the longest cooldown either champion has in lane, and by far the largest window the entry could hand the player. Crippling Strike at 5s and Decimate at 9-5s frame the short trades.
audit.corrected: Apprehend's 16-26s written into the cooldown breakdown, whys[1] and mid; Crippling Strike's 5s reset named as the burst tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) Decimate is called 'his passive Q' in spikes[0], early and wants.foe[2]; the passive is Hemorrhage, Decimate is the Q. (b) A Hijacked Noxian Guillotine is sold as scaling 'with your AP' and hitting hard — Sylas cannot apply Hemorrhage, so the stolen copy fires at base true damage with no stack bonus. (c) Crippling Strike's auto-attack reset is never given as the tell.
audit.why: The Guillotine claim is the dangerous one: a player promised a heavy execute will commit to a fight expecting damage that will not arrive. Riot's R text scales its damage per Hemorrhage stack on the target, and nothing in Sylas's kit applies that bleed.
audit.corrected: Decimate named as the Q and Hemorrhage as the passive; the stolen Guillotine restated as base true damage that still resets on a kill; the Crippling Strike wind-up named as the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, though the outer ring of Decimate heals him off every champion it hits and the entry's own losing condition is his sustain.
audit.why: Anti-heal timing is what decides whether the levels 4-5 attrition stretch is survivable.
audit.corrected: Named in whys[3] and mid as the answer to the outer-ring heal.

audit.why: The packet flags wants.you[2] 'Steal Noxian Guillotine' as a suspect name. False positive — that is the real ability.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Darius's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: His Guillotine at five bleed stacks beats your stolen copy, which carries no Hemorrhage — bait his R out first.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend (Pull): matchup-defining — The pull starts every Darius kill pattern — bait it before stepping up. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E1 shield for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Darius Apprehend: matchup-defining — the pull starts every kill pattern and it is 16-26s, the longest gap in the lane. Bait it, then step up. - Crippling Strike resets his auto on 5s. - Grievous Wounds answers Decimate.

edits.before: The pull starts every Darius kill pattern — bait it before stepping up. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: The pull starts every Darius kill pattern — bait it, then commit inside the 16-26s gap, never into it.

edits.before: Your E is now live but so is his Apprehend — a hook from you is a trading opportunity but a pull from him is a death sentence, so only use E2 after he wastes his E.
edits.after: Your E is live but so is Apprehend — your hook is a trade, his pull is a death sentence, so move up only once he has spent it and eaten its 26s cooldown.

edits.before: Darius hits his pre-6 peak: outer-ring Q heals him through your W and five-stack Hemorrhage plus Guillotine is a near-guaranteed kill if you overstay — respect the bleed counter on your screen.
edits.after: Darius hits his pre-6 peak: Decimate's outer ring heals him through your W unless you have Grievous Wounds, and five Hemorrhage stacks make his execute near-guaranteed if you overstay — watch the bleed counter.

edits.before: Hijacking Noxian Guillotine completely reverses the execute dynamic — bait him into a trade, get him to half HP, then fire his own R for true-damage; the reset on kill means one clean fight can snowball.
edits.after: His Guillotine is the bigger threat at 6: yours carries no Hemorrhage stacks, so it lands base true damage. Bait his out, then use your copy as the finisher — it still refreshes on a kill.

edits.before: Darius's passive Q outer edge stacks Hemorrhage for free — he shreds your HP before you can get E online, so give up the first wave entirely.
edits.after: Decimate's outer edge stacks Hemorrhage for free and heals him — he shreds your HP before E is online, so give up the first wave entirely.

edits.before: Hijack steals Noxian Guillotine; with your AP it deals true damage and resets on kills, letting you flip the execute threat back onto Darius.
edits.after: Hijack steals Noxian Guillotine: base true damage only, since you cannot apply Hemorrhage — but it still refreshes on a kill, so use it as the finisher.

edits.before: Zone you off CS with passive Q range so you never get full enough HP to safely hook in
edits.after: Zone you off CS with Decimate's outer ring so you never get healthy enough to hook in

edits.before: Darius owns level 1 completely — his passive Q outer ring stacks Hemorrhage from range and you have no dash to punish him yet. Farm from the tip of your Q and do not step inside his Q ring for any CS. At level 2 your E comes online but his E Apprehend is also live; if he pulls you in you eat a full empowered Q to the face, so only use E2 to hook after he whiffs his E or is clearly out of range. Keep the wave even or slightly slow-pushed so you are never trapped at turret where his bleed ticks kill you.
edits.after: Darius owns level 1 completely — Decimate's outer ring stacks Hemorrhage and heals him, and you have no dash to punish it yet. Farm from the tip of your Q and never step inside that ring for CS. At level 2 your E comes online but Apprehend is live too; get pulled and you eat the empowered Q to the face, so hook only after he whiffs it and owes 26 seconds. Keep the wave even or slightly slow-pushed so you are never trapped at turret where the bleed finishes you.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 you have your full kit but Darius is at his strongest — five-stack Hemorrhage plus the outer-ring Q heal means extended trades crush you even with W. Look for single short rotations: E1 dash forward to bait the Apprehend, let him whiff, E2 hook onto him, Q slow into one passive auto, W immediately, then E1 out before bleed ticks up. Never let him get a free pull and never stand still once bleed is stacking. Level 6 is the turning point: hijack Noxian Guillotine and bait him into trading into you at low HP — your stolen R deals true damage and resets, which means you threaten the exact execute he was relying on.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 you have your full kit but Darius is at his strongest — five Hemorrhage stacks and the outer-ring heal crush extended trades even through W, so buy Grievous Wounds before you contest them. Look for single short rotations: E1 forward to bait Apprehend, let him whiff and owe 16-26s, recast to pull onto him, Q slow into one Petricite auto, W immediately, then leave before the bleed stacks. His Crippling Strike wind-up is the cue to step out, not the cast. At 6 he is still favoured: his Guillotine carries five stacks and your stolen one carries none, so bait his out before you commit yours.

edits.before: Post-first-item the lane levels out into a genuine skill contest. Your Riftmaker Omnivamp stacks through the same extended fights Darius wants, and a stolen Guillotine at 6 has already shifted who threatens whom. In teamfights Noxian Guillotine in your hands is a hard-hitting true-damage execute that resets freely — coordinate with your team, steal it before every dragon or baron, and use it to clean up whoever Darius was supposed to kill. One-versus-one late you still have to respect his bleed, so lead with W damage and keep the fight below 20 seconds so Hemorrhage never reaches execute threshold.
edits.after: Post-first-item the lane levels out into a genuine skill contest. Your Riftmaker Omnivamp stacks through the same extended fights Darius wants, and by two items you are the better teamfighter. In teamfights a stolen Guillotine is base true damage rather than the stacked version he fires, but it refreshes on a kill and ignores resistances — steal it before every dragon or baron and use it to clean up whoever he was supposed to finish. One-versus-one late you still have to respect the bleed: lead with W damage and keep the fight short so Hemorrhage never reaches five stacks.

notes: The most misleading line in the entry was the stolen-Guillotine promise: 'with your AP it deals true damage' invites the player to commit expecting Darius-sized execute damage, when he cannot apply Hemorrhage and so fires the base version. The mirror reached the same conclusion independently. Apprehend's 16-26s is the single most useful number this lane could carry and appeared nowhere. Level 6 flipped to Darius per the mirror, and whys[4] and phases[4].why were rewritten together so the chart and the text now say the same thing.
